description:
We bring humanity's silent lunar and Martian hardware to life through interactive storytelling. By turning NASA's mission data into engaging visual narratives, we show how discarded rovers and landers paved the path for space exploration.

​Why Join Us? Work on a creative space-history project, build a standout portfolio piece, and earn an official NASA certificate.

​Skills Needed: Content Writers (scripts), Visual Designers (UI/UX, art), Researchers (NASA data), and Web Developers.
summary:
Ghost Fleet Archaeology is an interactive, browser-based cartographic web application that maps and tells the stories of humanity's dormant scientific hardware left behind across the Moon and Mars. Built using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Leaflet.js, the platform transforms raw planetary coordinate data into an immersive exploration experience featuring widescreen surface image overlay, glowing star beacons, and a telemetry-inspired interface.

The project addresses the challenge of making off-world exploration history accessible and engaging by curating over 20 historical artifacts—including Apollo surface experiments, impactors, landers, and robotic rovers—into a single unified dashboard. Clicking any beacon reveals high-resolution imagery, mission stories, and scientific achievements.

By preserving the locations and legacies of these mechanical pioneers, Ghost Fleet Archaeology bridges planetary science with cultural heritage, inspiring future explorers while highlighting the enduring engineering milestones that paved the way for modern spaceflight.
details:
Ghost Fleet Archaeology is an interactive web-based planetary mapping platform that allows users to explore historical hardware left behind by humanity on the Moon and Mars. Users can toggle between lunar and Martian global viewports, inspect glowing star coordinate beacons, and click any marker to open a glassmorphic telemetry drawer containing archival photography, mission backstories, landing years, and key scientific discoveries.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:
- Frontend: HTML5, CSS3 (custom glassmorphism and neon telemetry styling), and vanilla JavaScript (ES6+).
- Mapping Engine: Leaflet.js configured with custom widescreen image overlays (`maxBounds` locked to a 16:9 coordinate ratio) and custom `L.divIcon` markers.
- Deployment & Version Control: Git, GitHub, and Vercel for continuous cloud hosting.

Creativity, Impact & Design Factors:
Rather than presenting spaceflight history as static text tables, our team designed the interface like an orbital archaeological command center—giving each lander, rover, and impactor a first-person narrative voice ("Ghost Fleet"). We carefully considered user accessibility and visual clarity by spacing coordinates across the planetary grid to prevent marker overlap, building responsive side drawers, and hosting local image fallbacks to guarantee fast, reliable loading for educators, students, and space enthusiasts worldwide.
